item.title: Author Post
item.content:encoded:
Thank you to the following critics:

  • Ellie3
  • Elementa Chemiae (offsite)
  • Uncle Nicolini
  • alyvia (offsite)
  • UraniumEmpire
  • OthellotheCat
  • Ralliston
  • Dysadron
  • kinchtheknifeblade
  • Nagiros
  • Ayumi-san
  • MaliceAforethought

Hhh, okay. Well, it's up. I think this tale is going to be rather controversial, and furthermore I am bracing myself for it sinking. However, I figured there was little else to be edited about this tale, and it will either sink or swim, and it's best if I just toss it into the water and let it sort itself out so it can be out of my brain.

Hopefully the content warning makes it very explicitly clear that the viewpoint depicted isn't my own. It's a bit icky that I even have to specify that, but I understand the times we live in are as icky as anything. Ick.

Hope you enjoy it. Well, enjoy is probably not the right word. I might have more to put into this author post later. For now, I have to go to work.

EDIT: I indeed have more to say here, now that I am sure this is going to stay up, huzzah! I would first like to say that, yes, you're not crazy, this is, in a way, a rewrite of I Don't Get It, But I'll Figure It Out. by Uncle Nicolini. Hence the name similarity, and even some lines I lifted straight from that text, just to make the connection really solid. This started as a rewrite intended to replace the original, before Nico and I realized it was going such a completely different direction that it ought to be made into its own thing (not to mention just how many people clearly really like the original). The idea came about once Nico and I realized that his tale didn't accurately represent Fae and Tim's relationship as portrayed in the What a Wonderful World canon.

I'd also like to set aside time in this author post to acknowledge something: as a cis guy, this really isn't my story to tell. It was pretty much happenstance that ended up with me writing something this… I don't have an adjective. Something this. I accept that if the majority opinion is that this is harmful representation of the genderqueer experience, it will cease to exist, as that is more important than most anything. If I'm so prideful as to ignore this outcome as it comes about, call me on it and refer to this post, I can (and do) get very attached to my own writing. However, this tale seems to be faring well, I have high hopes, I just wanted to acknowledge the lowered position I am placing myself in, to write this tale. If that makes any sense at all.

Anyhow, that's all. Go read Nico's tale as a pick-me-up after the discomfort that is this version!
